claim: Qualcomm's FY2025 10-K explicitly names Apple for the first time as a disclosed revenue concentration, stating that Apple, Samsung, and Xiaomi each comprised 10% or more of Qualcomm's consolidated revenues in fiscal 2025.
stance_target: Forward margin effect of in-house modems / scale of Apple's importance to Qualcomm
scope_conditions: Qualcomm fiscal year 2025 (ended Sep 28, 2025), SEC Form 10-K, Item 1 Business
quoted_support: In fiscal 2025, revenues from Apple, Samsung and Xiaomi each comprised 10% or more of our consolidated revenues.

claim: Qualcomm's 10-K states as a formal, legally-reviewed risk factor that Apple's shift to its own modem products will have a 'significant negative impact' on Qualcomm's QCT (chip) segment revenues, results of operations and cash flows -- repeated verbatim across three separate risk-factor sections (customer concentration, vertical integration, and competition).
stance_target: Forward margin effect of in-house modems
scope_conditions: Qualcomm FY2025 10-K, forward-looking risk factor language
quoted_support: We expect that Apple will increasingly use its own modem products, rather than our products, in its future devices, which will have a significant negative impact on our QCT revenues, results of operations and cash flows.

claim: Qualcomm's 10-K discloses that Apple purchases only Qualcomm's 'thin modem' (MDM) products, excluding integrated application processor technology, which carry lower revenue and margin contribution per unit than Qualcomm's combined modem-plus-application-processor products sold to other customers.
stance_target: Composition of the Qualcomm-Apple relationship prior to full modem displacement
quoted_support: Apple purchases our MDM (or thin modem) products, which do not include our integrated application processor technology, and which have lower revenue and margin contributions than our combined modem and application processor products.

claim: In Qualcomm's anonymized customer-concentration table (Note 2), the largest single customer/licensee accounted for 21% of total revenue in FY2025, down from 22% in FY2024 and 27% in FY2023 -- a declining trajectory over three years consistent with, though not confirmed by the filing to be, Apple's modem-share erosion given Apple's named 10%+ status and the known start of Apple's in-house modem shipments (iPhone 16e, early 2025).
stance_target: Forward margin effect of in-house modems (magnitude and trajectory)
scope_conditions: Qualcomm consolidated revenue, FY2023-FY2025; customer identity is NOT disclosed by name in this table, only inferred from cross-reference with Item 1's named-customer disclosure
quoted_support: Revenues from each customer/licensee that were 10% or greater of total revenues were as follows: ... Customer/licensee (x) 21% 22% 27%

claim: Qualcomm's QCT (chip) segment total revenue grew year over year in FY2025 despite Apple share erosion: $38,367 million (FY2025) vs $33,196 million (FY2024) vs $30,382 million (FY2023), with Handsets revenue specifically at $27,793 million (FY2025), $24,863 million (FY2024), and $22,570 million (FY2023) -- indicating non-Apple handset demand (Android/Chinese OEMs) more than offset the early-stage Apple modem transition within the fiscal year covered.
stance_target: Whether Apple's modem displacement is already visible in Qualcomm's reported segment financials
quoted_support: QCT revenue streams were as follows (in millions): ... Handsets 27,793 24,863 22,570 ... Total QCT revenues 38,367 33,196 30,382

claim: Qualcomm's 10-K frames vertical integration by large customers (naming Apple and Samsung specifically) as a top-tier risk factor to its semiconductor business, expecting these customers to increasingly use their own integrated circuit products rather than Qualcomm's across some or all of their devices.
stance_target: Owning silicon is load-bearing for margin (from the displaced supplier's own disclosed perspective)
quoted_support: Certain of our largest mobile handset customers (for example, Apple, Samsung and Xiaomi) develop their own integrated circuit products, which they have in the past utilized, and/or currently utilize, in certain of their devices. We expect such customers will in the future utilize their own integrated circuit products in some or all of their devices, rather than our products.
